title: Copy, Clone and Cow
concept: Implicit duplication, explicit cloning and lazy ownership

writing.summary: Ask which bytes are shared, copied or allocated before choosing an ownership conversion.
writing.explanation:
`Copy` permits implicit duplication of a value. `Clone` is an explicit operation whose cost and semantics depend on its implementation. Cloning an `Rc` or `Arc` normally creates another owner of the same allocation; cloning a `String` normally creates owned string storage. The word `clone` alone does not tell you which one happened.

`Cow` stores either borrowed or owned data behind one interface. A borrowed `Cow<str>` can read a caller’s string without making an owned `String`. Requesting mutable access through `to_mut` converts the borrowed form into owned storage when needed. The original borrowed string is not changed. If the `Cow` already owns a `String`, obtaining mutable access need not clone that `String` again.

The example starts with borrowed text, requests a modification and checks that the original remains unchanged. This is a useful API when many inputs pass through untouched and some need normalization. It is not a guarantee that every `Cow`-based design is faster: consider how often ownership is required and how long the borrowed source must live. State the input lifetime and resulting ownership clearly rather than advertising zero copies for every path.
writing.exampleCaption: Mutation converts this borrowed `Cow` into independent owned text.
writing.rule: `Clone` semantics depend on the type; `Cow` delays ownership conversion until an operation needs it.
writing.task: Explain the example, predict the result, and justify your answer to the follow-up.
writing.success: Identify the relevant ownership or API contract and test the changed constraint.
writing.question: What changes when `to_mut` is called on this borrowed `Cow<str>`?
answers: It mutates the original borrowed str in place.
It keeps a mutable reference into the original immutable str.
It obtains owned storage and mutates that owned value.
writing.feedback: The borrowed branch becomes owned before mutation. `Cow` does not bypass `str`’s immutability or the lifetime of a borrowed source.

depth.misconception: It mutates the original borrowed str in place.
depth.correction: A borrowed `Cow` cannot write through its `&str`. `to_mut` first clones the text into an owned `String` and mutates that, so `source` still reads `crab`.
